record.tranche_reason: Applies attention SAEs and transcoders to a small Othello move-prediction model and reports learned features, extending dictionary-feature evidence to this model and task. It does not test the original superposition intervention or measure overcomplete feature geometry.
record.gate_note: The study reports SAE/transcoder reconstruction and interpretable feature findings relevant to dictionary recovery (V4). It does not vary feature count, sparsity, or importance, or test polysemanticity, capacity pressure, or feature dimensionality. The 99.3% move-prediction accuracy is task performance, not a result about the claim; cited results from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The post trains attention SAEs and transcoders as tools to build a weight-based relevance graph of a 600k-parameter OthelloGPT. It reports the dictionaries' loss recovered (tool quality) and qualitative readings of features along its own relevance tree. It never asks whether the model holds more sparse features than dimensions, whether neurons are polysemantic, or whether dictionary features are canonical. There is no control, no baseline (e.g., neuron basis or random dictionary), and the subject is not a natural-language LLM. So it relies on dictionary recovery rather than testing V4 or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The author calls this a preliminary report: attention SAEs plus transcoders and a weight-only relevance metric give an end-to-end computational graph. The u_A1 graph shows pattern-building decision trees and an inhibitory feature, which the author offers as evidence that patch-free methods can yield interpretable graphs at scale. Causal confirmation by activation patching is left to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses attention SAEs and transcoders with a weight-based upstream relevance metric to analyze OthelloGPT-small; it does not reproduce Toy Models of Superposition or measure superposition geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Transcoder features in a 3-layer, 128-dim OthelloGPT were read as compound board-pattern (union) features and an inhibitory feature anti-aligned with the A1 unembed. The readings are qualitative and come from a weight-only relevance graph.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dictionary features in small game-playing transformers compose hierarchically into interpretable circuits, traceable from weights alone.

record.problems: The report is preliminary and focuses on one small, board-game model. The feature-pattern interpretations are qualitative, no controls or uncertainty estimates are reported, and the author says activation patching could confirm the proposed circuits in future work.
record.rows_left_out: The 99.3% legal-move accuracy and the comparison with the original OthelloGPT are task-capability results, not findings about dictionary feature recovery or superposition. Claims attributed to cited studies are also excluded.
record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' and its V4 'supports' label are dropped. The dictionaries are used as an instrument, and their loss recovered is method performance, not evidence about superposition. The subject is a tiny board-game transformer, not an LLM. The interpretations have no controls or uncertainty. LessWrong post, not peer reviewed.

versions.untested_parts: No test of more sparse features than dimensions, overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
No test of neurons sharing features due to limited capacity, or of important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
No test of polysemanticity or alternative causes of it.
Tests SAE/transcoder feature recovery only in OthelloGPT-small on a board-game task. It does not test feature distribution across neurons or recovery in natural-language LLMs.
No test of whether dictionary features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
No test of whether features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: OthelloGPT-small

rows.measure: Feature activation pattern and relation to the unembedding vector
rows.value: The feature was described as activating on A1-legal boards except when predicting the final move, and as inhibitory to the A1 logit; the text gives cosine similarity below -0.95 and p(legal|feature active) above 0.5.
rows.note: The proposed function is a hypothesis; the author says similar features appeared in graphs for other unembedding nodes.
rows.check: The inhibitory-feature description (cos < -0.95 with the unembed; p(legal|active) > 0.5) characterises one circuit component. It does not bear on superposition or dictionary recovery as a claim.
